$comment: Pinned upstream snapshot of the vendored anti-slop Oxlint plugin. Upstream is private:true and publishes no npm package, so vendoring is the only integration path and this file is the substitute for a version range. Refresh with: ANTI_SLOP_UPSTREAM=<checkout> node --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/drift.test.ts --update
$kinuComment: Rules authored here, not vendored: they encode Kinu policy and have no upstream counterpart. Named explicitly rather than inferred from `kinuOnly` so an upstream-tracked rule cannot be demoted out of byte comparison without appearing in this list. `kinuRuleGates` partitions them across the *.gate.test.ts files that prove each one red->green through the real oxlint binary; drift.test.ts asserts the partition is exact, so adding a rule without a gate fails. Both lists cover PLUGIN rules only. `typescript-escapes.gate.test.ts` is deliberately absent from them: it gates `.oxlintrc.json` policy for two oxlint BUILT-INS (typescript/no-explicit-any, typescript/ban-ts-comment), which have no rule file here to author or pin, and naming a built-in in kinuRules would claim authorship of upstream code and break the partition drift.test.ts asserts. It is listed under `vendored` as kinuOnly because every file in this directory must be declared.

index.ts.reason: Registers the Kinu-local rules declared in kinuRules beside the pinned upstream rules. Upstream has no counterpart for these policy rules.

rules/no-runtime-typeof.test.ts.reason: Upstream's suite lists `typeof x === "undefined"` existence probes as valid (commit f2a8e0b); the local rule rejects every typeof, so those four cases are invalid here.

rules/no-runtime-typeof.ts.reason: Adds the objectInstanceof check with scope-aware resolution of the global Object binding (via the shared resolveVariable): `x instanceof Object` is the same evasion as typeof and upstream has never rejected it at any commit. Declines upstream's isExistenceProbe carve-out (commit f2a8e0b), which accepts `typeof x === "undefined"`: a binding whose presence is unknown is boundary input, and `globalThis.x === undefined` probes it without a typeof. Upstream's allowInTypeGuards option is vendored as-is and .oxlintrc.json does not set it, so no typeof exception is active.

rules/no-shape-in-symbol-names.test.ts.reason: Upstream's suite lists `schema.shape.id` (a non-computed member of an external value) as valid; the local rule rejects it, so those cases sit in `invalid` here alongside the case-insensitive substring cases that pin the ban against being narrowed to a lexical word (30 hidden violations, 2026-08-17).

rules/no-shape-in-symbol-names.ts.reason: Declines upstream's isBorrowedMemberName carve-out (commit f2a8e0b), which stops reporting `owner.shape` when the identifier is a non-computed member of another value. A member named shape is still a symbol named shape, whoever owns the object; the tree carries none, so the ban stays total. Bytes are upstream's pre-f2a8e0b rule.

rules/no-unknown-parameters.test.ts.reason: Upstream's suite lists `cause: unknown` and type-predicate subjects (`value: unknown): value is string`) as valid; the local rule rejects both, so those cases are invalid here, and alias-resolution cases (scoped, generic, chained aliases to unknown) pin what the local rule adds over upstream's literal-union match.

rules/no-unknown-parameters.ts.reason: Resolves aliases through upstream's shared type-alias environment (scoped, generic and chained aliases to unknown) and grants no exemption: upstream exempts a parameter named `cause` and, since commit 63d6966, the subject of a type predicate. Both carve-outs let unparsed boundary input through unflagged. Upstream's union/parenthesis handling (containsUnknownType) is subsumed by the alias resolution here.

rules/no-unsafe-dictionary-type.test.ts.reason: Upstream's suite lists four type-parameter-constraint dictionaries as valid; the local rule rejects them, so those cases are invalid here.

rules/no-unsafe-dictionary-type.ts.reason: Declines upstream's isInsideTypeParameterConstraint carve-out (commit 63d6966), which accepts `<T extends Record<string, unknown>>`. The constraint is the contract every caller of the generic is held to, so a dictionary there is the same unparsed-shape claim as one on a parameter. Everything else (scoped and generic alias resolution via visibleTypeAlias) is upstream's.

rules/require-safety-comment-for-type-as.reason: Adds unverifiableAssertion (a comment cannot establish a caller-selected generic, recover evidence from `any`, or validate raw JSON.parse output) and insufficientSafetyComment (a SAFETY note must name concrete evidence: three words and an evidence verb, where upstream since 63d6966 requires only a non-empty justification). Upstream's markers option and export-declaration comment attachment (f2a8e0b) are vendored as-is; .oxlintrc.json sets no markers.

$notVendored: Upstream files deliberately outside the vendored set, so their absence is policy rather than drift. (1) `src/effect/` (five opt-in Effect rules and shared/tagged-values.ts): Kinu imports `effect` in no file, so every one of those rules would register and fire on nothing; a rule that measures an empty set proves nothing and would inflate the rule count the ladder reports. Vendor them the day an `effect` import lands. (2) `src/rules/no-array-filter-map.ts` (+ suite): rejected on measurement, not taste. It fired 152 times on this tree (2026-09-10, oxlint 1.78.0), and both replacements its message prescribes are slower on both engines this tree runs on. Measured with a throwaway microbenchmark over {id, active} rows, half kept, n=8/64/1024/65536: `.values().filter().map().toArray()` ran 6.7x/7.7x/8.7x/2.0x the cost of `.filter().map()` on Node 22 (V8, the workerd engine) and 9.5x/6.5x/6.1x/4.4x on Bun 1.4 (JSC); `flatMap(x => keep ? [x] : [])` ran 3.4x/4.4x/4.9x/1.2x on V8 and 2.0x/3.4x/3.8x/3.1x on JSC. The iterator form also does not typecheck under this tree's ES2022 libs. Only a hand-written push loop is faster (0.5x-0.8x), which the rule does not propose and which would trade 152 declarative sites, nearly all over fixture, config and JSX lists of a few dozen elements, for loops. Re-measure before adopting. (3) `src/rules/require-readable-spacing-cli.test.ts`: spawns `pnpm exec oxlint`, and this tree has no pnpm; the rule is proven through the real oxlint binary here by live-tree.gate.test.ts over every governed file and its fixes by rules/require-readable-spacing.test.ts. `src/shared/lexical-type-parameters.ts` IS still vendored: upstream keeps it beneath shared/type-alias-resolution.ts.
